description:

**Gap this closes**: sp:06-analyze coverage analysis (2026-09-23) found zero beads task creates this module. FR-001 requires every fenced ```syml block in SYML-SPECIFICATION.md that states an Output or an ERROR to produce/raise exactly that from loads(). SC-001 requires the count (53 today) to track the specification as it is edited. The hand-transcribed Gherkin acceptance suites (US01-US09, all already written) satisfy the ATDD loop but are transcribed from spec.md's Acceptance Scenarios, NOT extracted from SYML-SPECIFICATION.md's fenced blocks (R-08: 'distinct jobs') — so all US1-US9 acceptance scenarios passing does NOT by itself satisfy FR-001/SC-001. This module is the only thing that does.
**Behavior**: At pytest collection time, read SYML-SPECIFICATION.md, find every fenced ```syml block immediately followed by an **Output:** line (JSON — assert loads(src) == json.loads(expected)) or an **ERROR:** line naming an exception class (assert pytest.raises(getattr(syml, exception_name))). Parametrize one test case per block. Assert a minimum block count of 53 (per SC-001 and research.md R-08's stated guard) so a regex-drift bug that silently finds zero blocks fails loudly instead of passing vacuously.
**Placement**: tests/test_spec_examples.py (plan.md file tree, ~L266). Lives under tests/ — inside the mypy file set, outside the coverage gate (pyproject's coverage config covers src/ and tools/ only). Runs in the ordinary unit suite (uv run pytest), NOT under just acceptance and NOT requiring pytest-bdd. No subprocess/shell-out needed, so no ruff S40x/S60x noqa is required (unlike the US9 bindings).
**Existing patterns**: existing files under tests/ for this repo's pytest style (see pytest-unit-testing skill — mypy-typed test functions, -> None, fixtures typed, ruff preview/pydocstyle). Use pytest.mark.parametrize with ids derived from block position/line number for readable failure output.
**Skills**: /pytest-unit-testing
**Discovery rule**: if a parametrized case fails (a fenced block's stated Output/ERROR does not match), that is a real conformance gap distinct from the hand-transcribed acceptance scenarios — file a new Red/Green/Refactor sub-chain under the relevant US<N> parent (not under this task, not under US9) to fix the underlying src/ behavior; do not weaken this test or hand-tune the extractor to skip the block.

**Commit**: /sp-commit then git push.

title: Red: inline key/list-item values mark TextLeafNode.inline True
description:
**Type**: RED (write failing test)
**Story**: US1 — Tree building follows the specification's acceptance rules
**Behavior**: An inline value (text on the same line as its key or list marker, e.g. 'a: Note') must set TextLeafNode.inline=True so its continuation baseline stays open (None) until the first accepted continuation line fixes it (D11), rather than being fixed at the inline text's own column. description: US8 acceptance scenarios (specs/acceptance-specs/US08-source-tracking.feature: BOM, CRLF, U+2028) require as_source() positions for UNQUOTED leaves and keys in original-text coordinates, not just quoted values (syml-x0m.5.9.11-13). Currently SymlNode.__post_init__ (src/syml/nodes.py) and KeyLeafNode.key still call Source.from_node(pnode, filename=...) with no line/position_map, so they fall back to Pos.from_str_index over the NORMALIZED document text. parse() (src/syml/parsers.py) now threads a PositionMap into SymlParser (syml-x0m.5.9.12), but only visit_quoted_value uses it. Notes for whoever picks this up: (1) Source.from_node's line/position_map path assumes pnode.start is LINE-LOCAL (pos_at(line, offset) = Pos(line.start+offset, ...)), but the current grammar (lines = line*) parses the whole normalized document in one pass, so pnode.start is document-absolute — either derive a per-node Line from full_text (mirroring the Pos.from_str_index(full_text, pnode.start) + position_map.to_original(...) approach used in visit_quoted_value) or restructure to per-line parsing invocation.
